subtopics.title: What Development Means and How It Is Measured

questions.question: Development differs from economic growth because:
options: Growth is more output countable in currency, while development asks whether the output becomes health, schooling, choice and dignity
Growth applies only to farms and development to factories
Development is measured in money and growth is not
They are two names for the same measurement

questions.question: GDP and GNI per capita share the weakness that:
options: They cannot be calculated for developing countries
As averages, a per-person figure is silent about who actually pockets the money
They ignore all economic production entirely
They count only agricultural output

questions.question: South Africa's Gini coefficient matters because:
options: It shows the country has the world's largest economy
It counts only rural incomes
Among the highest recorded anywhere, it measures the extreme inequality behind the golf estate fenced beside the shack settlement
It proves average incomes are falling

questions.question: A fair treatment of Rostow's model includes the criticism that it:
options: Contains too few stages to be memorable
Applies only to island economies
Was designed to describe city growth, not countries
Assumes every economy climbs the West's staircase, ignores colonial history and late-starter handicaps, and treats arrival at wealth as guaranteed

subtopics.title: Trade, Aid and the Rules of the Game

questions.question: The terms of trade trap raw exporters because:
options: Primary prices lurch and drift downward against manufactured prices, so the same trainload of ore buys fewer machines each year
Raw materials cannot legally be exported
Manufactured goods always fall in price
Shipping costs rise only for finished goods

questions.question: Beneficiation is the recognised escape from the trap because it:
options: Removes all tariffs on raw exports
Processes materials at home so the value added is captured locally — selling the jewellery, not just the gold
Doubles the volume of ore exported
Replaces mining with tourism entirely

questions.question: The developing world's oldest grievance about trade rules is that:
options: Free trade has been abolished everywhere
Tariffs no longer exist in any country
Wealthy countries preach open markets while subsidising their own farmers so heavily that African producers are undercut at home
Multinational corporations refuse to trade with Africa

questions.question: The balanced conclusion of the aid debate is that:
options: All aid should stop immediately
Aid should always be tied to donor purchases
Emergency aid causes dependency and must end
Aid succeeds when it builds capacity and answers local priorities — and the deeper cure is fair trade and investment, not charity

subtopics.title: Powering the Country — Conventional and Non-Conventional Energy

questions.question: The coal chain from seam to socket runs:
options: Coal milled and burned, heat raising superheated steam, steam spinning the turbine, turbine spinning the generator, cooling towers exhaling waste heat
Coal dissolved in water, filtered, then electrified
Coal burned inside the transmission lines directly
Steam cooled first, then heated by the generator

questions.question: Pumped-storage schemes like Drakensberg and Ingula are best described as:
options: The country's largest true hydro-electric sources
Giant water batteries — pumping uphill in quiet hours and generating at the evening peak, consuming more than they produce
Desalination plants for inland provinces
Backup coal stations with water cooling

questions.question: The auction mechanism that built South Africa's renewable fleet:
options: Nationalised all private power stations
Guaranteed fixed profits regardless of price
Set private developers bidding competitively, drawing in billions and driving wind and solar prices below new coal
Applied only to nuclear procurement

questions.question: The honest weighing of renewables includes:
options: No weaknesses of any kind
Higher fuel costs than coal every year
Carbon emissions equal to thermal stations
Clean, fuel-free and cheapest — but intermittent, needing storage, backup, a stronger grid, and a just transition for coalfield towns

subtopics.title: Soil, Sustainability and the Greener Economy

questions.question: The erosion ladder runs:
options: Bare ground, raindrop splash, sheet erosion, rills, then gullies — the dongas that end a field's farming life
Gully first, then rills, then sheetwash, then splash
Wind, then water, then ice, then gravity
Contour, terrace, rotation, gabion

questions.question: The verbatim definition of sustainability is:
options: Recycling all waste produced by a country
Meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own
Growing the economy faster than the population
Using only renewable energy sources by law

questions.question: In the greener economy, government's assigned responsibilities include:
options: Auditing the energy use of private households
Installing solar panels on every factory roof itself
Charting the path away from coal, running renewable procurement, enforcing standards, taxing carbon and managing the just transition
Choosing which appliances citizens may own

questions.question: The circle that joins the year runs:
options: Soil feeds coal, coal feeds rivers, rivers feed trade
Trade causes storms, storms cause aid, aid causes energy
Development is unrelated to energy or soil
Development needs energy; coal energy spends water and warms the climate; the climate loads droughts and storms; storms strip soil; lost soil starves the farming development promised to feed

subtopics.title: The Scoreboard and the Rigged Shop

questions.question: The three fixes to the school-report problem of GDP are:
options: Count per person, check the spread with Gini, and follow the money into lives with the HDI
Double the total, halve the average, ignore the spread
Count exports only, then imports only, then both
Replace GDP with the balance of trade

questions.question: In the rigged shop, wealth pools wherever:
options: The rawest materials are dug
The MAKING happens — finished goods climb in price while raw prices wobble and sag
The most customers live
The shop's charity counter operates

questions.question: Bread against bakeries summarises the aid debate as:
options: Bread deliveries are always harmful in every case
Bakeries should be nationalised by donors
Emergency bread is right when the flood strikes, but aid that builds bakeries beats aid that delivers bread — and fairer shop rules would beat both
Only bilateral aid can build bakeries

subtopics.title: The Braai Fire and the Two Free Fuels

questions.question: The braai fire's genuine virtues are:
options: Cheap local fuel, jobs, and the steady all-night heat a grid needs as baseload
Zero emissions and zero water use
Instant startup and shutdown at will
Fuel that renews itself each morning

questions.question: The two free fuels cannot simply take over tomorrow because:
options: Their electricity is the most expensive available
The sun knocks off at dusk and the wind takes unscheduled leave — and a country cannot take leave from electricity
South Africa lacks any usable sun or wind
Renewable plants take longer to build than coal stations

questions.question: The dam that doubles as a battery works by:
options: Storing chemical batteries below the dam wall
Desalinating seawater during off-peak hours
Pushing water uphill at midnight with cheap power and letting it fall through turbines at supper time
Generating power from evaporation

questions.question: A complete answer on the energy switch must include the people of the fire because:
options: Miners operate the wind turbines already
Coal towns have no stake in the outcome
Electricity prices do not affect households
Whole coalfield municipalities live on coal wages, so a just transition must retrain workers, build new industry in place, and give communities a stake in the replacement

subtopics.title: Living Off the Interest — Soil and the Sustainable Year

questions.question: In the banking rule for sustainability:
options: Soil is capital and the harvest its interest — erosion is spending capital and booking it as income
The harvest is capital and soil the interest
Coal is interest arriving fresh each day
Sun and wind are capital being burned once

questions.question: Coal and sunshine differ in the banking picture because:
options: Both are renewable interest payments
Coal is pure capital — a once-off inheritance going up in smoke — while sun and wind are pure interest, deposited fresh every morning
Sunshine is a loan that must be repaid
Coal regenerates in the seams each century

questions.question: The repair list for the teaspoon account includes:
options: Deep ploughing straight down every slope
Removing all vegetation to expose fresh soil
Cover on the ground, contour furrows as tiny dams, terraces, rested and rotated veld, matched herds, and gabions across existing dongas
Concreting over eroded fields

questions.question: Walking the circle of the year means showing that:
options: Each topic stands alone and must be revised separately
Physical geography has no link to human geography
Only energy and trade are connected
Development, energy, climate and soil form one loop — and sustainability is the habit of inspecting every link before acting
